angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 482,816 km at 71.40 pc = 0.09 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 14.0065 +/- 0.0176 mas (same row, RUWE 1.16): 71.40 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.694 +/- 0.021 solar radii from Bakos et al. 2010, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HAT-P-20 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2010arXiv1008.3388B/abstract): 482,816 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.756 +/- 0.028 solar masses from Bakos et al. 2010, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HAT-P-20 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2010arXiv1008.3388B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4595 +/- 80 K from Bakos et al. 2010, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HAT-P-20 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2010arXiv1008.3388B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bakos et al. 2010, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HAT-P-20 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2010arXiv1008.3388B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hat-p-20.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.634, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
